correctness.rationale: The identity closure is a closure operator and the generator is defined from the independently specified Kripke semantics on N. At n the box tests the fixed row S[n] contained in N; at z it tests cofiniteness of the operand's truth set on N. A formula true at all worlds belongs to every generator, and the row condition and the cofinite condition each preserve modus ponens. Inductively, the k-fold box of bottom is true at n exactly when n<k, since for k>=1 the test at positive n uses 0 and n-1. Thus chi_j is false only at j among the ordinary worlds and belongs to the z generator. To exclude z from the common core, not-box-chi_0 is true at all positive n because 0 is a successor and falsifies chi_0, but is false at z because chi_0 is cofinite there. The common core is therefore empty with bottom absent from the generator, contradicting KRep. A preserving Kripke relation would have no z successor and therefore wrongly make box-bottom true. Every operand's truth value on N stabilizes by structural induction; in the box case the truth value at n>=1 is the conjunction of the value of its operand at 0 and n-1. For any finite Phi choose one m beyond all box-operand cutoffs, keep every S row, and set R_Phi[z]={m}. The box case then agrees at z for every subformula examined; N never points to z, so its truth is unchanged. This verifies simultaneous agreement at every world for each finite Phi, not the existence of a single relation for all Phi. The checker was inspected, not executed; its finite-prefix tests are only corroborative.
residual_risks: The argument is about preservation on the same carrier with the same valuation, not extensions by an ideal point.

evidence: The finite-world representation criterion and census assume finite carriers. The infinite countermodel in Nishimura uses identical cofinite generators at every world and atom valuations cofinite except a parity letter. The image-finite strict-order Kripke model in Hansen–Kupke–Pacuit has unbounded row sizes, unlike the fixed bound two.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the finite representation theorem nor the more general infinite nonrepresentation example implies this existence statement with its stronger language and row restrictions.

evidence: Cofinite-filter finite realization by a finite set of successors is itself a general observation: restrict to the intersection of the finitely many positive cofinites and select a witness for each negative noncofinite test. With all rows cofinite as in Nishimura the same construction can be used at all rows for finite subformula sets. The new model instead has one exceptional row, and one successor suffices simultaneously for all its finite tests by eventual constancy. A nonrelational operator on all subsets does not automatically imply nonrepresentability on definable truth sets.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The result is not credited for these general consequences of a cofinite filter alone. The low-degree atom-free carrier defines the necessary witnesses and excludes the exceptional point itself, which is not an automatic consequence of the compared examples.

evidence: The obstruction is an empty intersection of all truth sets of accepted box operands, despite rejection of bottom. Nishimura realizes this by valuation letters naming complements of singleton worlds. Hansen–Kupke–Pacuit realize finite satisfiability without a global witness with all atoms false in a different augmented neighbourhood example over the strict order.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The comparison credits the mechanisms under their other formulations, but distinguishes the modal singleton definitions and exceptional-world separator needed for a variable-free model with sparse ordinary rows.

value.rationale: For the concrete representation problem it matters whether new worlds, extra propositional names or large branching are responsible for failure. This witness removes the need for names and high branching, and any finite all-world observation fails to detect the global obstruction even under same-carrier approximation. That pinpoints the distinction between a cofinite family of locally realizable requirements and one world realizing them globally.
residual_risks: The value is a sharp example, not a classification of infinite representability or a completeness theorem.
